learning_outcomes.text: Identifies and explains the elements that make up a projection system in descriptive geometry;
Identifies and explains the elements that define different projection systems used in engineering graphic representations such as conical, parallel axonometric projection;
Identifies and explains the projections of the point, line, and plane in the double and triple orthogonal projection system;
Identifies and explains the remarkable lines and planes in the double and triple orthogonal projection system;
Identifies and explains the Methods of descriptive geometry;
Identifies and explains the representation of polyhedra, as well as how to determine a planar section in them or how to determine the result of the intersection between two polyhedra;

Identifies and explains the projection of conical and cylindrical surfaces, as well as how to determine sections made in them or how to determine the result of the intersection between two such surfaces.
Uses classic tools for graphic representations;
Correctly represents points, lines, planes, and surfaces in the drawing (epure);
Determines the curves resulting from the sectioning of polyhedral or cylindrical-conical surfaces with a plane;
Can construct the development of a polyhedral or conical surface;
Determines the curve/curves resulting from the intersection of two polyhedral surfaces or two cylindrical-conical surfaces.

Respects the principles, norms, and ethical values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in making decisions for solving assigned tasks;
Integrates into the workgroup and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels;
Continuously informs and documents themselves in their own field of activity by appropriately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques;
Develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Projection systems. The Point: Object, importance, and history of descriptive geometry. Projection systems. Projection systems used by computer-aided graphics programs. Representation in double and triple orthogonal projection of the point. Descriptive coordinates. Representation of points using computer-aided graphics programs.

The Line: Double orthogonal projection of the line. Regions of the line. Triple orthogonal projection of the line. Remarkable lines. Relative positions of two lines. Representation of lines/line segments in computer-aided graphics programs.
The Plane: Representation. Traces of the plane. Determining the plane from different conditions. Remarkable positions of the plane. Relative positions of two planes. Line and plane.
Methods of Descriptive Geometry: Method of changing projection planes. Rotation method. Rabattment method.
Polyhedra: Representation, point on surface. Planar sections in polyhedra. Development of polyhedra. Intersections of polyhedra.

Conical and Cylindrical Surfaces: Representation, point on surface. Tangent planes. Planar sections in cone and cylinder. Intersection of conical and cylindrical surfaces (Method of inscribed spheres).
Methods of describing object geometry in CAD systems: Two-dimensional models. Three-dimensional models.

Drawing of epures in double and/or triple orthogonal projection in cases related to the study of points, lines, and planes. Graphic calculation aiming to determine them in epure from different conditions.
Test on chapters: point, line, plane.
Drawing of epures in the case of representation, sectioning, and development of polyhedra.
teaching_methods: Explanatory and participatory lectures based on PowerPoint presentations

assessment_methods.method: Formative evaluation test from chapters related to the study of the point, line, and plane
Summative evaluation test from the chapter reserved for the study of polyhedra

Active participation in laboratory work by providing answers and solutions to the proposed problems (all laboratory assignments must be completed, with recovery of only one outstanding laboratory assignment allowed)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its corresponding study credits. Conditions for promotion include the ability to correctly draw points, line segments, and planes in the epure, and knowledge of methods for describing objects in CAD systems.
